_metadata.primary_source: Jegham et al. (2025), How Hungry is AI? Benchmarking Energy, Water, and Carbon Footprint of LLM Inference, arXiv:2505.09598 (v6, Nov 2025 — 30 models, DEA eco-efficiency ranking)
anchor_sources: Google (Aug 2025), Measuring the environmental impact of delivering AI at Google, arXiv:2508.15734 — median Gemini Apps text prompt: 0.24 Wh, 0.26 mL water, 0.03 gCO2e (market-based, incl. embodied)
OpenAI / Altman (Jun 2025), The Gentle Singularity — average ChatGPT query: ~0.34 Wh, ~0.32 mL water
Mistral AI (Jul 2025), lifecycle analysis of Mistral Large 2 (ISO 14040/44, peer-reviewed) — 1.14 gCO2e and 45 mL water per 400-output-token response (full lifecycle)
Epoch AI (Feb 2025), How much energy does ChatGPT use? — ~0.3 Wh per typical GPT-4o query; ~2.5 Wh at 10k-token input

Oviedo et al. (Microsoft), Energy Use of AI Inference, arXiv:2509.20241 (PREPRINT v1 figures: median 0.34 Wh/query, IQR 0.18-0.67, >200B-param models in production; non-production extrapolations overstate 4-20x). VERSION UNPINNED: the published Joule (2026) version reports different values and was NOT read in this pipeline - verify against the journal article before quoting any figure from it.
URI AI lab / Jegham dashboard (Aug 2025) — GPT-5 medium reasoning response: ~18.35 Wh average, up to ~40 Wh (contested estimate)
Adamska et al. (2025), Green Prompting, arXiv:2503.10666 — response length is the dominant energy driver (r~0.9); input length matters far less

notes.tier_field: On reference entries only: which tier of unmeasured closed models this entry is evidence for (small or frontier). The tier estimator takes the median of its members' fitted coefficients as the point and their spread as the range (PLAN.md Step 2, METHODOLOGY §2.5).
notes.thinking_pair_field: On a reference thinking entry: the non-thinking sibling it pairs with. The energy one adds beyond the other, in the sibling's decode tokens, is evidence for how many hidden tokens thinking adds (METHODOLOGY §2.5). A measured open-weight thinking entry needs no pair: its plain answer is priced by the active-parameter estimator instead. deepseek-r1 is deliberately not paired with deepseek-v3, whose extrapolated decode coefficient is ~3.4x below EcoLogits' figure for the same architecture and would inflate R1's implied thinking ~3.5x.
notes.status_field: current = a model a user can pick today: released on or after 2026-01-01 and still its provider's current offering (PLAN.md Step 5). reference = an older entry kept as evidence for the estimators and so stored history can re-score; resolvable by id, never listed in a picker (engine listModels() returns current entries unless asked for reference ones).
notes.thinking_field: always = every answer reasons (hidden chain-of-thought is part of the benchmark energy); adaptive = the model decides how much to think; optional = the user can switch it on; none = no hidden reasoning.
notes.sources_field: Per-fact provenance. fact lists what the source vouches for, comma separated, from: name, released, params, precision, thinking, effort, tier, open_weight, status, pricing. status fetched = a primary page was opened on checked_on; search-only = only seen in search results or secondary sources. A current entry's estimate needs a fetched source for each fact it rests on: params and thinking for active-params (and precision, when one is stated; with none stated the estimate assumes 16 bits, which errs high, but only up to 200B total parameters, the range the estimator was fitted on); tier and thinking for tier. Otherwise the entry waits (PLAN.md Step 9, scripts/check-catalog.js).
notes.superseded_by_field: On a reference entry: the id of the model that replaced it, whose own chain must end at a current model; or null when it is history-only. Required on every reference entry once the catalog holds a current model (PLAN.md Step 9).
notes.data_source_field: measured = benchmarked in Jegham et al.; extrapolated = estimated from size class, hardware, and measured siblings; anchored = calibrated against a provider-reported per-prompt figure; estimated = no benchmark points at all: the engine derives the figures from the reference entries through the entry's estimate block (METHODOLOGY §2.5), and the apps show them as a range with the method named
notes.benchmark_configurations: short = 100 in / 300 out, medium = 1000 in / 1000 out, long = 10000 in / 1500 out tokens
notes.reasoning_models: Benchmark energy for reasoning models includes hidden chain-of-thought tokens at a typical thinking budget; the engine scales the fixed and decode terms (everything except prefill) for low/standard/high effort.
notes.provider_reported_anchor: A provider's own published per-prompt figure, kept for reference. Each anchor states its boundary; anchors with a wider boundary than the engine (full lifecycle incl. training, or a median prompt of unknown length) are not expected to be reproduced by the engine and are labelled as such.
evidence_gaps_2026_09_24: No lab has published a per-query energy figure for ANY 2026-generation model. Every 2026 entry is necessarily extrapolated, with no provider anchor.
Jegham et al. (arXiv:2505.09598) is unrevised at v6 (24 Nov 2025) - there is no v7.
Google has published no successor to its Aug 2025 figure of 0.24 Wh / 0.26 mL / 0.03 gCO2e per median Gemini Apps prompt.
Only the Llama and DeepSeek entries are open-weight enough for a genuine third-party measurement; closed hosted models are 'benchmarked', not measured.
notes.linearity_validity: The fitted coefficients are supported only across 100-10,000 input tokens - the range of the benchmark points. e_in is small but non-zero for every model (0.0009-0.516 mWh/token), so extrapolating it into 200k-1M context windows would attribute ~96% of a long query's energy to input, inverting Adamska et al. (arXiv:2503.10666), which this catalog cites for output-dominance. The engine therefore holds the input term flat past 5x the largest fitted point and flags the result as clamped.
notes.anthropic_lineup_2026_09_24: Anthropic's current lineup is Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5 and Haiku 4.5 (verified against Anthropic's own platform docs). Only Sonnet 5 is added here. Opus and Fable are DELIBERATELY ABSENT: no defensible energy figure exists for them, and seeding them from Sonnet's points would report a smaller, non-thinking model's number under a larger always-on-thinking model's name - repeating the exact understatement this release fixes. Until a measurement exists they resolve to no catalog entry, which the UI reports as such. UPDATE 2026-10-20: Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 now enter as estimated entries (tier method, with thinking priced as hidden tokens), never with Sonnet's benchmark points; Sonnet 5 becomes a reference entry superseded by Sonnet 5.5.
notes.roster_2026_10_20: The 2026 roster (PLAN.md Step 5). Every key fact was opened on the vendor's own pages: Anthropic's docs, and the labs' own GitHub repositories (SDKs, model catalogs, cookbooks, model cards), since the other vendor sites were unreachable from the build environment. Waiting until a primary source can be read: DeepSeek V4 (only secondary sources), Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B (no published precision, and at 2.4T it is past the 200B the estimator was fitted on, so 16 bits cannot be assumed), Gemini 3.1 Pro (still a preview id), Gemma 4 E4B (total parameters unpublished), Mistral Large 4 (open weights not released). Until DeepSeek V4 enters, deepseek-v3 and deepseek-r1 point nowhere (superseded_by null).

_metadata.data_source_field: measured = an independent third-party hardware measurement (open-weight models only); benchmarked = estimated by the Jegham et al. infrastructure-aware framework, not instrumented - no third party can meter a closed hosted model; extrapolated = estimated from size class, hardware and measured siblings; anchored = calibrated against a provider-reported per-prompt figure; estimated = no benchmark points at all: the engine derives the figures from the reference entries through the entry's estimate block (METHODOLOGY §2.5), and the apps show them as a range with the method named

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5
models.notes: Benchmark points CARRIED FORWARD verbatim from Claude Sonnet 4.5 (same tier, same host). No lab has published a per-query energy figure for any 2026-generation model, so this is a transparent carry-forward, not a measurement of Sonnet 5. Named correctly so the reported number stops being attributed to a superseded model; the underlying figure is unchanged and equally extrapolated. Replace as soon as a measurement exists.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.5
models.notes: Legacy. Superseded by Claude Sonnet 5 and then 5.5; a reference entry kept so stored history stays resolvable.

models.name: Claude 3.7 Sonnet
models.notes: Absent from Anthropic's current model lineup. A reference entry: resolvable for stored history, never listed in a picker.

provider_reported_anchor.boundary: Median prompt of unknown length; on-site water only; market-based carbon incl. embodied — the engine's location-based, on-site + off-site figures are expected to be higher
provider_reported_anchor.label: Google-reported median Gemini Apps text prompt (Aug 2025, full-stack measurement)

provider_reported_anchor.boundary: Cradle-to-grave LCA including training amortisation and embodied hardware — a far wider boundary than the engine's inference-only estimate, so these figures are ~25× higher than the engine's and are not comparable

models.name: GPT-6 Sol
models.notes: Superseded in the API by GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI: "If you already use gpt-6-sol, review the migration guidance before switching to GPT-6.1 Sol"). Kept as a reference with its estimate so ChatGPT detection and stored history still resolve. released is the date OpenAI's Python SDK added the id (its CHANGELOG); OpenAI's launch page could not be opened from the build environment.

models.name: Muse Spark 1.3
models.notes: Meta's API defines reasoning_effort "none" but says it "isn't reliably available yet on the public endpoint", so thinking counts as always on (errs high). Meta publishes no size or price; the tier is frontier, as Meta's own HackBench calls it a "frontier proprietary" model. Released in September 2026: Meta's cookbook moved to muse-spark-1.3 "ahead of the 1.3 release" on 2026-09-02.

models.name: Muse Spark Open
models.notes: Meta ships two checkpoints: BF16 (the reference, ~1.65 TB) and NVFP4 (mostly 4-bit, ~537 GB). The estimate uses BF16, the larger, so any error runs high. Reasoning cannot be turned off; xhigh is the default. Released 2026-10-15, the date of the vLLM launch post Meta links.

models.name: Muse Glimmer 30B
models.notes: 30B dense decoder (the text model is ~29B). Meta's reference weights are BF16. Meta's llama.cpp recipe says reasoning cannot be turned off; the template's default strength is high. The release date is Together's, as quoted in Meta's cookbook.

models.name: Grok 4.7
models.notes: xAI lists reasoning efforts low, medium, high (the default) and xhigh, with no "none", so thinking counts as always on. xAI calls it "the most capable model". Released by 2026-09-22: it is in xAI's generated model list from that day's docs snapshot. The API's multi-agent model is grok-4.20-multi-agent, not a 4.7 id.

models.name: Kimi K3
models.notes: MoE expert weights are MXFP4 (quantization-aware training); the other components stay in higher precision, a small share of the weights. Thinking is always on; reasoning_effort low, high or max, default max. Released July 2026: Moonshot's repo was created on 2026-07-27 (+0800).

models.name: GLM-5.3
models.notes: The main checkpoint ships in FP8 (a separate BF16 repo exists). reasoning_effort low, high or max, default max; Z.ai documents no way to switch thinking off for 5.3, so it counts as always on (errs high). Released August 2026: Z.ai's README added GLM-5.3 on 2026-08-27 (+0800).

models.name: GLM-5.3-Flash
models.notes: The main checkpoint ships in FP8 (a separate BF16 repo exists). reasoning_effort low, high or max, default max; no documented off switch, so thinking counts as always on (errs high). Released August 2026: Z.ai's README added it on 2026-08-26.

models.name: Qwen3.8-27B
models.notes: 27B from Qwen's own model name; with no A-suffix it is taken as dense, all 27B active (errs high if it is not). No weight precision is published, so 16 bits is assumed (errs high). Thinking counts as always on, as for the 2.4T model.

models.name: Mistral Small 4
models.notes: 119B total, 6.5B active, as Mistral counts it. Mistral lists GPU memory at bf16, fp8 and fp4 but not the shipped precision, so 16 bits is assumed (errs high). Reasoning is adjustable with reasoning_effort.

models.name: Mistral Medium 3.5
models.notes: 128B total and 128B active: dense. No shipped precision is published, so 16 bits is assumed (errs high). reasoning_effort none or high; Mistral's Vibe defaults to it with thinking high (levels off and high).

models.name: Nemotron 3 Ultra
models.notes: Hybrid Mamba-attention MoE. NVIDIA ships BF16 (the reference) and NVFP4 checkpoints; the estimate uses BF16, so any error runs high. The precision table is from a summary of the official card in NVIDIA's own repo. Reasoning is on by default and can be switched off. Released June 2026: NVIDIA added it to its repo on 2026-06-04. No first-party chat host, so it runs on aws (PLAN.md Step 4).

models.name: Gemini 4 Argon
models.notes: Thinking levels low, medium (the default) and high; no minimal and no thinking budget, so thinking cannot be switched off. Released 2026-10-13: Google added it to its SDK and cookbook that day (SDK release 2026-10-14).

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash
models.notes: Google: thinking is always on, but Gemini 3 Flash models accept minimal, "roughly equivalent to off", so the range starts at no thinking. high is the Gemini 3 default. Released 2026-09-02, the day Google's SDK added it.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite
models.notes: Google's thinking guide covers Gemini 3 Flash models in general (always on, minimal roughly off, high by default); no statement names Flash-Lite alone. Released 2026-07-21, the day Google's cookbook added it.

models.name: Gemma 4 26B-A4B
models.notes: Parameter counts from Google's size label "26B A4B" (a mixture of experts); the model card with exact counts is on a host the build environment cannot reach. No shipped precision is published in Google's repos, so 16 bits is assumed (errs high). Thinking is switched on with enable_thinking. Runs on google_cloud: no first-party chat host (PLAN.md Step 4).

models.name: Gemma 4 31B
models.notes: 31B from Google's size label; dense (no mixture-of-experts settings in Google's model code). No shipped precision is published, so 16 bits is assumed (errs high). Thinking is switched on with enable_thinking. Runs on google_cloud.
